subject: Mutual action playbook: Nimbus Health POC - GPU reservation & eval timeline
messages:
From: Alice Becker <alice.becker@nimbushealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Mutual action plan and capacity lead times for Nimbus POC

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to move from tech eval to a short POC. Procurement asked me to capture an initial mutual action plan (MAP) that includes explicit timelines for procurement and any capacity reservation we should plan for (Dedicated or Private). High-level asks from our side: 

- A proposed 6–8 week evaluation window with milestone gates.
- Minimum GPU footprint we should reserve to avoid throttling during eval (we expect bursts during data ingest and long-context trials).
- Lead times for Redwood Dedicated pools vs. Private/VPC install (we need to align with our procurement and infra windows).
- Any temporary burst/bank options if we need extra capacity during the eval spike.

Attached: nimbus_poc_requirements.pdf — includes expected request QPS and sample prompt lengths. Can you share a short MAP draft and a sizing recommendation by EOD Wednesday so we can align internally?

Thanks,
Alice Becker
Head of ML Ops, Nimbus Health
procurement@nimh.com

[attachment: nimbus_poc_requirements.pdf (PDF, 120 KB)]

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Alice Becker <alice.becker@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan and capacity lead times for Nimbus POC

Alice — appreciate the clear ask. Drafting a concise MAP and sizing note for you — attached is a working spreadsheet (RW-draft-MAP-Nimbus-v1.xlsx). Key points up front: 

- Proposed eval window: 8 weeks (2 weeks ingest/bench + 4 weeks model eval + 2 weeks integration/stability). Milestone gates: data ingest complete, latency baseline validation (<100ms p95), cost-per-100k tokens estimate signoff.

- Recommended reserved capacity (starting point):
  * Staging pool: 4 x A10 (40T equivalent) for day-to-day evaluation traffic.
  * Spike buffer (burstable): capacity to scale to 12 x A10 equivalents (or 4 x A100-80GB equivalents) for heavy prompt/regeneration runs.
  * Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) recommended if PHI ingestion is required — lead time ~6–10 weeks due to infra and KMS integrations.
  * Dedicated reserved capacity: can be provisioned in ~2–3 weeks if customer commits to a CR (monthly reserved pool).

- Short-term options: we can offer a temporary burst quota from our shared hosted pool during peak days to avoid blocking the eval (limited and metered).

Next steps I propose: quick sync Thursday to walk the MAP, then I’ll convert the draft into a MAP that includes milestone owners, success criteria, and procurement checklist. Can you confirm availability?

Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

[attachment: RW-draft-MAP-Nimbus-v1.xlsx (Excel, 45 KB)]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan and capacity lead times for Nimbus POC

Adding some infra specifics from the infra & dedicated team side (copying Lauren for procurement coordination):

- Dedicated pool sizing notes: our experience with similar healthcare POCs shows 1 A100-80GB or 3x A10 equivalent usually covers heavy context runs, but time-to-first-byte sensitivity favors A100 for long-context experiments.

- Lead times: 
  * Dedicated (reserved) — if customer signs a 3/6/12 month reservation we can allocate and test the dedicated pool in ~10 business days after contract finalization (assuming standard onboarding credentials and no network isolation requirements).
  * Private (VPC) — typical end-to-end: 6–10 weeks (network, KMS, infra provisioning, security review). If the customer uses a preferred cloud partner, we can shorten to ~4–6 weeks with a prioritized channel.

- Sizing guidance: propose baseline staging of 4x A10 equivalents + 2x A100 reserved headroom for model calibration. Suggest a canary schedule during week 3 to validate KV-cache behavior at production-like sequences.

- Cost / commitment trade-offs: suggest discussing a modest initial commit (1–2 months) to secure Dedicated capacity and then move to a 6-month ramp if the POC metrics look good.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions — Dedicated Products
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: Alice Becker <alice.becker@nimbushealth.com>

Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, Tom Li <tom.li@nimbushealth.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 14:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan and capacity lead times for Nimbus POC

Thanks — this is very helpful. A few clarifying items from procurement and infra: 

- Procurement wants an explicit lead-time commitment for Dedicated if we sign a short-term (60 day) reserved contract. Can you confirm the 10 business day start after contract execution? We may need that in our procurement checklist.
- For Private/VPC, our infra lead wants a tighter window if possible — can Redwood work with our cloud partner to compress to 4–6 weeks? If so, we will prioritize that route.
- Burst option: procurement asked whether a metered burst from Redwood hosted pool can be contractually guaranteed during 2 scheduled spike days in the eval window. If you can offer that with a cost uplift, please include it in the MAP.

Also looping Tom (infra) — Tom, can you confirm whether PHI will be part of the POC? If yes we’ll move toward Private.

Best,
Alice

Alice / Tom — thanks for the clarifying Qs. Attached is the finalized mutual action playbook (Nimbus_MAP_v1.xlsx) with explicit milestone owners, dates, and procurement checklist. Highlights: 

- Dedicated lead-time: confirmed 10 business days after contract countersignature to provision & smoke-test a reserved pool (we’ll commit in the MAP to that SLA).

- Private/VPC: we can target 4–6 weeks if Nimbus engages your cloud partner and shares a prioritized onboarding window; otherwise standard is 6–10 weeks. We’ll include an explicit onboarding timeline and KMS steps.

- Burstable hosted option: yes — we can commit to 2 scheduled spike days during the eval and provide metered burst capacity from our hosted pool at an agreed uplift rate. I’ve added the uplift table and sample billing calculation to the MAP.

- Sizing recap: start with Staging = 4x A10 equivalents; Spike headroom = up to 12x A10 equivalents (or 4x A100-80GB equiv) for scheduled stress tests. Canary schedule set in week 3.

Next steps: 
1) Please review the attached MAP and confirm owners on your side by Tuesday (8 Dec).
2) If procurement is ready, we can send a limited DocuSign for the initial 60-day reserved commit (link below) — once countersigned we’ll begin the 10-business-day provisioning cadence.
3) Share a PO or procurement timeline so Lauren can align billing and onboarding.
